A.notes:
The orgaization of content on the Activity Charts page, below the secondary nav and above the cards, looks off. It did not use the sort bar, and I think a 'show more' link for the categories is the wrong affordance because it gives the first categories more precendence. A better element choice would show or hide all of them. It also looks strange to have the line for categories aligned left followed by the filter and sort button, aligned right. It looks like a misalignment even though it is not. 

The refresh button should hav an icon and be grouped with the text about the time it was last updated. On desktop, it wraps to a second line and there is no icon, though there is a gap that makes it look like an icon was intended to go there.

B.notes:
The refresh button is missing an icon.

On the activity charts page, the only improvement over the previous page is that the sort dropdowns are aligned left so it does not look misaligned with the list of categories. But, as in build A, I think the show more link is the wrong affordance for the categories list. And it did not use a sort bar.

C.notes:
On the all sections page, the icon is added to the refresh button, yay! That button should be grouped with the text about when it was last updated, though (this applies to all of the builds. maybe it is how we presented the content for the page).

I am concerned about the decision to put the categories accordion at the bottom of the activity charts page. Normally this page will have a long list of visualizations so it will take a lot of scrolling to get to it. I am more and more convinced that some sort of tooltip or modal is the right solution. It is a menu that, when you need it you want to see all the options, but when you don't then you want all options tucked away.

This build also did not use the sort bar.

D.notes:
It has no "refresh" button on the all sections page.

On the activity charts page, it did not use the sort bar and left out the list of categories altogether.

The accordiong for 'about these charts' is pushing the primary content down further and getting too much prominence. It is becoming clearer to me, with my human review, that there is a space for modals in this page layout. So far no agent has tried that affordance. I wonder why?

together:
Accept/Reject is not a good measure of improvement or even of quality. My standards are changing as the builds are improving, so I am rejecting more now that earlier, even though the layouts have improved. What is the purpose of that voting mechanism for you? If it is to learn from what worked and what didnt then maybe what we need is that, on the final page showing all of the builds, I select the one that in my opinion is best and the one that is worst. 

I also noticed that all of the builds treated the line on the first page about the time period as a footnote. That is great. Did the spec tell them to do that, or did they figure out that it was a lower priority piece of information because of some change to the docs? 

This set of builds did not use the sort bar for some reason. Why do you think that is?
